Q: Best approach for timeline preview in a video editor using Media3 CompositionPlayer A:

CompositionPlayer is a useful API for simple compositions and demos, but I would not currently rely on it as the core of a production-grade video editor.

The main reason is that timeline editing is a very different workload from media playback. During editing, operations like trim, split, move, insert, and delete happen frequently, which means the composition graph changes continuously. CompositionPlayer was primarily designed for playback of a composition, not for rebuilding that composition dozens of times per second while the user is actively editing.

Professional editors such as CapCut, VN, or InShot typically do not rely on CompositionPlayer for their editing preview. Instead, they usually have their own timeline engine that maintains the project state and renders preview frames independently of the export pipeline.

A common architecture looks like this:

  • A timeline model containing clips, audio tracks, overlays, transitions, etc.

  • A rendering engine that determines which video frame should be displayed for the current timeline position.

  • A dedicated audio mixer to mix multiple audio tracks into a single synchronized output.

  • A lightweight preview renderer (often based on OpenGL ES or Vulkan) for video frames and overlays.

  • A separate export pipeline that renders the final composition offline.

In this architecture, ExoPlayer is often used only as a media decoder or source of frames, not as the timeline engine itself.

If you're staying within Media3, I would recommend:

  • Use a single ExoPlayer for decoding the currently visible video.

  • Keep your own timeline model rather than rebuilding a Composition after every edit.

  • Treat overlays as part of your rendering layer instead of recreating the playback graph.

  • Use CompositionPlayer only if your composition changes infrequently.

If your editor requires:

  • frequent timeline edits,

  • frame-accurate seeking,

  • multiple parallel audio tracks,

  • smooth scrubbing,

  • real-time overlays,

then a custom timeline/rendering engine is generally a better long-term solution than trying to synchronize multiple ExoPlayer instances or rebuilding CompositionPlayer continuously.

In short, CompositionPlayer is currently better suited for playback of relatively static compositions than for implementing the editing preview of a professional non-linear video editor.

Q: How to remove space between curly braces `} }` while formating JavaScript in VS Code? A:

You can disable parameters using VS Code global configuration file settings.json:

"javascript.format.insertSpaceAfterOpeningAndBeforeClosingNonemptyBraces": false,
"typescript.format.insertSpaceAfterOpeningAndBeforeClosingNonemptyBraces": false

Q: Tree Shaking / Minifying Firebase using esbuild A:

From the connectAuthEmulator in your code it seems that you use a single build target for both development and release builds.

I recommend making a separate development build and only including connectAuthEmulator (and other dev dependencies, such as setupEmulators) in that one, so that your packaging tool can shake dev dependencies from the production builds.

Q: com.amazonaws.AmazonClientException: Unable to execute HTTP request: peer not authenticated A:

You have to determine

  • SECRET_KEY
  • ACCESS_KEY
  • END_POINT_URL

for authentication purpose. and use:

    AmazonS3 s3;
    AWSCredentials credentials = new BasicAWSCredentials(ACCESS_KEY, SECRET_KEY);
    s3 = new AmazonS3Client(credentials);
    s3.setEndpoint(END_POINT_URL);

now you can upload image using s3 object.
